```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo=FALSE, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE)
invisible(Sys.setlocale("LC_CTYPE", "C.UTF-8"))
library(data.table)
library(DT)
# R code here is ASCII only (HTML entities for special characters), so the page renders the same in any locale
A <- "docs/assets/ctwas_gtex_SCZ_Brain_Cerebellum"
tq <- fread(file.path(A, "tissue_qtls.tsv")); st <- fread(file.path(A, "isoform_steps.tsv")); it <- fread(file.path(A, "isoqtl_steps.tsv"))
dc <- fread(file.path(A, "isoqtl_copies.tsv"))
pa <- fread(file.path(A, "params.tsv")); g <- fread(file.path(A, "gene_pips.tsv")); cv <- fread(file.path(A, "convergence.tsv"))
RUNS <- c(es="eQTL + sQTL", esi="eQTL + sQTL + irQTL", i="irQTL only", est="eQTL + sQTL + isoQTL", t="isoQTL only")
TYPES <- list(es=c("eQTL", "sQTL"), esi=c("eQTL", "sQTL", "irQTL"), i="irQTL", est=c("eQTL", "sQTL", "isoQTL"), t="isoQTL")
fmt <- function(n) format(n, big.mark=",", trim=TRUE, scientific=FALSE)
fp <- function(x) vapply(x, function(z) if (is.na(z)) "NA" else format(signif(z, 2)), "")
cell <- function(x) fifelse(is.na(x), "&ndash;", sprintf("%.2f", x))
iso <- pa[run == "esi" & type == "irQTL"]; isq <- pa[run == "t" & type == "isoQTL"]
cb <- tq[tissue == "Brain_Cerebellum"]
g8 <- function(r) g[run == r & combined_pip >= 0.8, gene_name]
# one run's genes: a PIP column per QTL type only when the run has more than one type; isoQTL runs add the duplicate count
gene_table <- function(r, d) {
  d <- d[order(-combined_pip)]; x <- d[, .(gene_name, combined_pip=sprintf("%.2f", combined_pip))]
  if (length(TYPES[[r]]) > 1) for (k in TYPES[[r]]) x[[paste0(k, "_pip")]] <- cell(d[[paste0(k, "_pip")]])
  x <- cbind(x, d[, .(Traits=n_traits, `Top trait`=top_trait, `Top trait type`=top_type, `susie_pip (top trait)`=sprintf("%.2f", top_trait_pip), z=sprintf("%.1f", z))])
  if ("isoQTL" %in% TYPES[[r]]) x[, `isoQTL copies` := fifelse(is.na(d$top_isoqtl_copies), "&ndash;", as.character(d$top_isoqtl_copies))]
  paste(knitr::kable(x, escape=FALSE, align=ifelse(names(x) %in% c("gene_name", "Top trait", "Top trait type"), "l", "r")), collapse="\n")
}
```

# How we selected the tissue

We chose the brain tissue with the most isoform-ratio QTLs (irQTLs: QTLs for an
isoform's share of its gene's expression), since SCZ is a brain
trait. The counts are Pantry's conditionally independent cis-QTLs per GTEx v8
tissue (`gtex.separate_kdp.qtls.tsv.gz`, downloaded 2026-10-29).

```{r tissues}
d <- tq[brain == TRUE | rank <= 3][order(rank)]
knitr::kable(d[, .(Rank=rank, Tissue=gsub("_", " ", tissue), `Pantry code`=code, `irQTLs`=fmt(isoform_qtls),
  Isoforms=fmt(isoforms), Genes=fmt(isoform_genes), eQTLs=fmt(eqtls), `Splicing QTLs`=fmt(sqtls))], align="rllrrrrr")
```

- **Rank:** among all `r nrow(tq)` tissues, by the number of irQTLs. The
  table shows the top three tissues overall and every brain tissue.
- **irQTLs:** independent cis-QTLs; **Isoforms** and **Genes** are the
  isoforms and genes they belong to. **eQTLs** and **Splicing QTLs** are Pantry's
  expression and intron-excision QTLs in the same tissue, for comparison.

Brain Cerebellum has the most among brain tissues: `r fmt(cb$isoform_qtls)`
irQTLs in `r fmt(cb$isoforms)` isoforms of `r fmt(cb$isoform_genes)` genes.
Testis has the most overall. Pantry codes the two cerebellum tissues BRNCHA and
BRNCHB. Its covariate files have 209 samples for BRNCHA and 175 for BRNCHB, the
GTEx v8 sample sizes of Brain Cerebellum and Cerebellar Hemisphere, so BRNCHA is
Brain Cerebellum.

# How the runs were set up

- **GWAS:** PGC schizophrenia, `ieu-b-5102` (N = 127,906), z-scores harmonized to
  the UK Biobank (UKB) LD reference, as for the M-cTWAS paper.
- **eQTL and sQTL weights:** the paper's GTEx v8 PredictDB expression and splicing
  models for Brain Cerebellum.
- **irQTL weights** (our definition): one trait per isoform, from Pantry's
  independent cis-QTLs in Brain Cerebellum. They come from the genes significant
  in Pantry's permutation test, q < 0.05.
  - Each isoform's QTL is its strongest independent variant (smallest nominal p)
    among single-base variants in the UKB reference that are not
    strand-ambiguous.
  - The weight is that variant's effect on the isoform ratio (tensorQTL's
    slope); with one SNP per trait, only its sign matters.
  - Genes come from Pantry's own annotation. We used top QTLs, not Munro's
    prediction models.
- **isoQTL weights** (added 2026-11-04; models from the paper, the top SNP is ours):
  one trait per isoform, from the isoTWAS prediction models of
  [Bhattacharya et al. 2023](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41588-023-01560-2) for GTEx v8
  Brain Cerebellum ([Zenodo 8047940](https://zenodo.org/records/8047940)).
  - The paper's trait is one isoform's expression (Salmon, GENCODE v38), predicted
    from SNPs within 1 Mb by multivariate models fitted over all of the gene's
    isoforms. Only isoforms with cross-validated R<sup>2</sup> &ge; 0.01 are released.
  - The models are dense (median 471 SNPs per isoform). We kept one SNP per
    isoform: the SNP with the largest standardised weight (|weight| &times; genotype
    SD from the UKB reference), among single-base SNPs in the UKB reference that
    are not strand-ambiguous. This is the model's most influential SNP, not a QTL
    lead variant (the released files have no QTL statistics). It carries a median
    7.7% of its model's total standardised weight.
  - Genes are named from the paper's PredictDB mapping (as for eQTLs), else from
    Pantry's annotation.
- **Settings, as the paper's runs:** each QTL type is its own group, with protein-coding genes only and LD
  from the UKB reference. eQTL and sQTL weights are scaled (`scale_predictdb_weights`), the
  isoform weights (irQTL and isoQTL) are not (one SNP per trait). No thinning, one prior variance shared
  by all groups (`shared_all`), up to 5 signals per region (L = 5).
- **Five runs:** eQTL + sQTL (the paper's QTL types), eQTL + sQTL + irQTL,
  irQTL only (added 2026-11-03, to test whether the irQTLs
  carry signal on their own), and eQTL + sQTL + isoQTL and isoQTL only
  (added 2026-11-04). All use the same settings.
- **Not done yet:** merging regions, checking LD mismatch, and merging
  [duplicate isoQTL traits](#duplicate-isoqtl-traits).

```{r steps}
knitr::kable(st[, .(Step=step, QTLs=fmt(qtls), Isoforms=fmt(isoforms), Genes=fmt(genes))], align="lrrr")
```

The irQTL weights at each step. The last row is the weights. cTWAS then
keeps the isoforms of protein-coding genes whose QTL is in the GWAS:
`r fmt(iso$group_size)` traits.

```{r isoqtl_steps}
knitr::kable(it[, .(Step=step, `Isoform-SNP pairs`=fmt(rows), Isoforms=fmt(isoforms), Genes=fmt(genes))], align="lrrr")
```

The isoQTL weights at each step; the first row counts every isoform-SNP pair in
the released models. cTWAS keeps the protein-coding isoforms whose SNP is in the
GWAS: `r fmt(isq$group_size)` traits.

## What the tables and figures show

**Parameters**, the output of `summarize_param()`:

- **group_size:** molecular traits that reach cTWAS after matching to the GWAS and the LD reference.
- **group_prior:** the estimated prior probability that a trait (or a SNP) is causal.
- **group_prior_var:** the prior variance of a causal effect, shared by all groups (`shared_all`).
- **log_enrichment:** the log of a group's prior over the SNP prior, with its
  standard error; **enrichment_pval** is its p-value.
- **group_pve:** the proportion of SCZ variance explained by the group;
  **total_pve** sums all groups and SNPs.
- **prop_heritability:** a group's `group_pve` over `total_pve`, the slices of the
  pie charts.

**Convergence**, from `make_convergence_plots()`: the estimates at each iteration
of the parameter estimation (proportion causal &pi; is `group_prior`, effect size
&sigma;<sup>2</sup> is `group_prior_var`, enrichment is
&pi;<sub>G</sub>/&pi;<sub>S</sub>, and PVE).

**Gene-level PIPs:** `combined_pip` combines all of a gene's molecular traits and
QTL types with `combine_gene_pips()` (`by = "type"`, `method = "combine_cs"`,
`filter_cs = FALSE`). **eQTL_pip**, **sQTL_pip**, **irQTL_pip** and **isoQTL_pip** are the gene's
PIP from each QTL type; "&ndash;" means the gene has no trait of that type in a
fine-mapped region. The mapping table assigns each trait to its gene: the paper's
PredictDB mapping for eQTL genes and sQTL introns, Pantry's annotation for
irQTL isoforms, and the PredictDB mapping (else Pantry's) for isoQTL isoforms.

# Results

## Parameters

```{r params}
w <- merge(pa[type != "SNP"], pa[type == "SNP", .(run, snp_prior=group_prior)], by="run")[order(match(run, names(RUNS)), match(type, c("eQTL", "sQTL", "irQTL", "isoQTL")))]
knitr::kable(w[, .(Run=RUNS[run], group, group_size=fmt(group_size), group_prior=sprintf("%.5f", group_prior), `group_prior (SNP)`=sprintf("%.5f", snp_prior),
  group_prior_var=sprintf("%.1f", group_prior_var), `log_enrichment (log_enrichment_se)`=sprintf("%.2f (%.2f)", log_enrichment, log_enrichment_se),
  enrichment_pval=fp(enrichment_pval), group_pve=sprintf("%.4f", group_pve), total_pve=sprintf("%.3f", total_pve),
  prop_heritability=sprintf("%.5f", prop_heritability))], align="llrrrrrrrrr")
```

```{r isoqtl_note}
ij <- pa[run == "est" & type == "isoQTL"]; e0 <- pa[run == "es" & type != "SNP"]; e1 <- pa[run == "est" & type != "SNP"]
pt <- function(r, ty) pa[run == r & type == ty, group_pve / group_size]
```

**isoQTLs** (2026-11-04): unlike the irQTLs, the isoQTLs stay enriched when
eQTLs and sQTLs are in the same run.

- `log_enrichment` is `r sprintf("%.2f", isq$log_enrichment)` alone and
  `r sprintf("%.2f", ij$log_enrichment)` with eQTLs and sQTLs (`enrichment_pval`
  `r fp(ij$enrichment_pval)`); the irQTLs fall from
  `r sprintf("%.2f", pa[run == "i" & type == "irQTL", log_enrichment])` alone to
  `r sprintf("%.2f", iso$log_enrichment)`.
- In the joint run the isoQTLs take `r sprintf("%.1f%%", 100 * ij$prop_heritability)`
  of `total_pve`, and all molecular traits together
  `r sprintf("%.1f%%", 100 * sum(e1$prop_heritability))`, against
  `r sprintf("%.1f%%", 100 * sum(e0$prop_heritability))` with eQTLs and sQTLs only.
- Per trait the isoQTL signal is small: `group_pve` / `group_size` (ours) is
  `r sprintf("%.1e", pt("est", "isoQTL"))`, against `r sprintf("%.1e", pt("est", "eQTL"))`
  for eQTLs in the same run. The share is large because the group is large
  (`r fmt(isq$group_size)` traits).

## Gene-level PIPs

### Genes with combined_pip of at least 0.8 in any run

```{r overview}
gn <- sort(unique(g[combined_pip >= 0.8, gene_name]))
pick <- function(r, col) vapply(gn, function(x) { v <- g[run == r & gene_name == x][[col]]; if (length(v)) v[1] else NA_real_ }, 0)
o <- data.table(gene_name=gn, a=pick("es", "combined_pip"), b=pick("esi", "combined_pip"), c=pick("i", "combined_pip"), d=pick("est", "combined_pip"),
                e=pick("est", "eQTL_pip"), s=pick("est", "sQTL_pip"), t=pick("est", "isoQTL_pip"), u=pick("t", "combined_pip"))[order(-d)]
knitr::kable(o[, .(gene_name, `combined_pip (eQTL + sQTL)`=cell(a), `combined_pip (+ irQTL)`=cell(b), `combined_pip (irQTL only)`=cell(c),
  `combined_pip (+ isoQTL)`=cell(d), `eQTL_pip (+ isoQTL)`=cell(e), `sQTL_pip (+ isoQTL)`=cell(s), `isoQTL_pip (+ isoQTL)`=cell(t),
  `combined_pip (isoQTL only)`=cell(u))], escape=FALSE, align="lrrrrrrrr")
```

Columns 2&ndash;5 and 9 are `combined_pip` in each run; columns 6&ndash;8
split the eQTL + sQTL + isoQTL run's `combined_pip` by QTL type. "&ndash;"
means the gene was not in a fine-mapped region in that run, or has no trait of
that type.

### Duplicate isoQTL traits

```{r dup_setup}
dt <- dc[run == "t"]; d5 <- function(r) dc[run == r & copy_group == "5 or more copies"]
pair <- g[run == "est" & gene_name %in% c("PPIL2", "TMEM25")][order(-combined_pip)]
ar <- g[run == "est" & gene_name == "ARHGAP9"]
```

**Caveat (ours):** with one SNP per isoform, isoforms of the same gene often get
the same top SNP. Their predicted expressions are then the same trait (up to
sign), and cTWAS keeps them as separate traits. SuSiE splits a signal evenly over
such copies and `combined_pip` adds them back, so a gene with many copies gets
the prior of many traits.

```{r dup}
knitr::kable(dc[, .(Run=RUNS[run], `Copies per gene and SNP`=copy_group, `isoQTL traits`=fmt(traits), `Share of traits`=sprintf("%.0f%%", 100 * trait_share),
  `susie_pip sum`=sprintf("%.1f", pip_sum), `Share of susie_pip`=sprintf("%.0f%%", 100 * pip_share))], align="llrrrr")
```

- **Copies per gene and SNP:** how many of the run's isoQTL traits have the same
  gene and the same SNP (1 = no duplicate).
- **susie_pip sum:** the isoQTL traits' `susie_pip`, summed over fine-mapped
  regions; **Share of susie_pip** is its share of the run's isoQTL total.
- **isoQTL copies** (gene tables below): the copies of the gene's isoQTL trait
  with the largest `susie_pip`.

The copy groups take about the same share of `susie_pip` as of traits, so the
duplicates do not drive the group estimates above. They matter for single
genes. In the eQTL + sQTL + isoQTL run,
`r paste(sprintf("%s (combined_pip %.2f) rests on %d copies of its top trait, each with susie_pip %.2f", pair$gene_name, pair$combined_pip, pair$top_isoqtl_copies, pair$top_isoqtl_pip), collapse=", and ")`.
Their SNPs have GWAS |z| `r paste(sprintf("%.2f", abs(pair$z)), collapse=" and ")`
(p `r paste(fp(2 * pnorm(-abs(pair$z))), collapse=" and ")`), below genome-wide significance. ARHGAP9 rests on one isoform,
`r sub(".*__", "", ar$top_trait)` (susie_pip `r sprintf("%.2f", ar$top_trait_pip)`,
z = `r sprintf("%.1f", ar$z)`).

### By run {.tabset}

Genes with `combined_pip` of at least 0.5.

```{r gene_tabs, results="asis"}
for (r in names(RUNS)) {
  cat("#### ", RUNS[[r]], "\n\n", sep="")
  cat(gene_table(r, g[run == r & combined_pip >= 0.5]), "\n\n", sep="")
}
```

- **eQTL_pip** and the other PIP columns appear when a run has more than one QTL type.
- **Traits:** the gene's molecular traits in fine-mapped regions, over all QTL types.
- **Top trait:** the trait with the largest `susie_pip`: its ID (an eQTL gene, an
  sQTL intron or an isoform), type, `susie_pip` and z-score (z).
- **isoQTL copies** (isoQTL runs only): see [Duplicate isoQTL traits](#duplicate-isoqtl-traits).

DT::datatable(as.data.frame(g[, .(Run=RUNS[run], gene_name, combined_pip=round(combined_pip, 3), eQTL_pip=round(eQTL_pip, 3), sQTL_pip=round(sQTL_pip, 3),

**Code:** `long_read_RNA/15.ctwas_gtex_isoform/`:

- `0.build_isoform_topqtl.R`: the irQTL top-QTL weights and their mapping table.
- `3.fetch_isotwas_models.sh`: fetches the Brain Cerebellum isoTWAS models from
  Zenodo (only the byte range that holds them, on the login node).
- `4.build_isoqtl_isotwas.R`: the isoQTL top-SNP weights and their mapping table.
- `1.run_ctwas.R` and `.sbatch`: the five runs (QTL types `es`, `esi`, `i`, `est` and `t`).
- `2.summarize.R`: this page's tables and figures.
